name: eel
about: Chain ragdoll body for the giant eel (31-bone quadruped rig, same skeleton as the salamander). 7 ball-jointed capsules in one line: hips (root, spine0), chest_a, chest_b, head (with neck), tail_a, tail_b, tail_c. Bones without a body (spine1, spine3, ears, jaw) follow their parent bone in the scene graph. Every number is here; src/chain.mjs holds none.
legs_note: the eel's four legs are vestigial: they have NO body. hind_* bones hang off spine0 and front_* bones off spine4, so in the scene graph they are visual only and follow the hips and chest_a capsules.
placeholder_note: radii, masses, joint limits and motor scales are PLACEHOLDERS to tune on Dom's phone and the clips; only the bone positions are measured.
scale_source: Armagedom Web/src/data/creatureDefinitions.json giant-eel scale.model 0.9 (the skeleton is the salamander's, so the eel is about 0.95 m long and 0.2 m tall at this scale): bones and radii below are in model units, the row is in metres at this scale
mass_assumption: placeholder: a thick-bodied river eel about 0.95 m long and 5 cm across weighs roughly 1.5 to 3 kg; 2.1 kg total. The game data gives hp 90 and no mass.
inertia_source: data/ragdoll-role-table.json motor.inertia_multiplier (M1 finding), same value as the humanoid rows
hinge_flex_z_source: no hinge joints: an eel has no knees or elbows in this chain

segments.source: placeholder: root, spine0 to spine2 (spine1 rides on it)
placeholder: spine2 to spine4 (spine3 rides on it; the vestigial front legs follow it)
placeholder: neck to jaw (neck + head + jaw, ears ride on it)
placeholder: tail2 to tail3 plus 0.05 model units past the last bone

severable.note: tail_a joint removed; the three tail capsules fall free
head joint removed; the head capsule falls free
